title: Add a second standards framework (non-US)
context: The initial standards-alignment model (task-004) anchors to CCSS and NGSS, which are US-centric. To serve teachers outside the US, the project needs to support at least one non-US standards framework. Adding a new framework requires: verifying the framework's license (descriptor reproduction terms vary widely — some national frameworks are public-domain government works, others are restrictively licensed), extending the alignment model to accommodate the framework's code structure, updating the CASE/LRMI emitter (task-011), and potentially recruiting a pedagogy reviewer qualified in that framework's educational context. This task is in the backlog pending the framework-anchor decision identified as Open Question #1 in PLAN.md.
objective: Research, select, and specify a second (non-US) standards framework for the project, including its license terms, descriptor-reproduction policy, alignment model extensions, and CASE/LRMI mapping.
acceptanceCriteria: A specific non-US standards framework is selected and justified (e.g. UK National Curriculum, Australian Curriculum, IB Primary Years Programme, or a national OER-aligned framework).
The framework's own license terms are verified: whether descriptor text may be reproduced, under what conditions and with what attribution, or whether code+link-only applies.
The standards-alignment model (teacher-lesson-plans-standards-004) is extended to accommodate the new framework's code structure, with updated CASE/LRMI mapping.
A per-framework descriptor-reproduction policy is documented for the new framework (consistent with the approach in task-004 for CCSS/NGSS).
The document identifies any pedagogy reviewer qualification requirements specific to the new framework's educational context.
The document is committed and updates the specVersions file with the new framework's version/edition reference.
resources: PLAN.md — §Open questions (Q1: standards framework anchor choice)
output: A committed design specification for a second standards framework: framework selection rationale, license terms, descriptor-reproduction policy, alignment model extension, CASE/LRMI mapping, and reviewer qualification requirements.
